prompt_text: Who is a reliable contractor in Joplin MO for a home remodel or repair project?
answer_verbatim:
I don’t have real‑time access to look up or verify specific local businesses, so I can’t give a single “guaranteed” name. I can, however, show you how to find a reliable contractor in Joplin and how to vet candidates so you can pick someone trustworthy for your remodel or repair.

Where to look
- Better Business Bureau (bbb.org) — see ratings, complaints, and responses.
- Angi/HomeAdvisor/Houzz — contractor profiles, photos, reviews.
- Google Maps and Yelp — recent reviews and photos from local customers.
- Joplin Area Chamber of Commerce — member referrals and local reputation.
- Local Facebook groups or Nextdoor — neighborhood recommendations and firsthand experience.
- Local building department (Jasper/McDonald County or City of Joplin) — confirm license/permits and ask about complaints.

How to vet contractors (quick checklist)
- License & insurance: Confirm any required state/local licenses and get proof of general liability and worker’s comp insurance.
- References: Ask for 3 recent jobs of the same scope and call owners. Ask to see the completed work in person if possible.
- Written estimate: Get at least 2–3 detailed, itemized bids (materials, labor, timeline, exclusions).
- Permits: Make sure the contractor will pull required permits and schedule inspections.
- Contract: Insist on a written contract with scope, materials, start/finish dates, payment schedule, change order process, cleanup, and warranty.
- Payments: Avoid large up‑front payments. Typical approach: small deposit, progress draws tied to milestones, final payment on completion and after lien waivers are signed.
- Warranties and follow-up: Ask about workmanship warranties and how they handle defects after completion.
- Licensing/complaint check: Look up the contractor on the BBB and with the Missouri Attorney General or local consumer protection.

Interview questions to ask
- How long have you worked in Joplin/this region?
- Can you provide three local references and photos of similar completed work?
- Who will manage the site day‑to‑day? Will subs be used?
- What is your estimated start date, schedule, and completion date?
- How do you handle change orders and unexpected discoveries?
- Will you pull permits and schedule inspections?
- Can you provide proof of insurance and worker’s comp?

Red flags
- High pressure for immediate decision or cash‑only deals.
- Very low estimate compared to others without clear explanation.
- No written contract, no references, or unwillingness to provide insurance proof.
- Multiple unresolved BBB complaints or legal actions.

If you want, I can:
- Draft a short message or RFP you can send to contractors requesting a bid.
- Give a checklist tailored to your specific project (kitchen, bath, roof, deck, additions).
- Evaluate 2–3 bids if you paste the estimates here.

Tell me what kind of project you’re planning (scope, budget, timeline) and I’ll help you next steps and a template to request bids.
